newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge up to new record, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge up to new record, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted minor gains in subdued trade on Monday although profit-taking erased part of the early gains, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed at a sixth consecutive all-time high of 92,134.21, up 375.30 points, or 0.41 percent from Friday's previous record of 91,758.91, but down from a day's high of 92,896. It had surged 5.49 percent last week.
Trade volume was nearly halved to 18.54 trillion lira from Friday's record 35.89 trillion.
In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.9, unchanged from Friday and compared to a record of $1 on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
"The index's drop was prevented by buying in bluechip Eregli and a few other utilities. But activity mostly focused on minor shares today," said Haldun Sertel from Can securities.
"However, I don't think the market can keep these gains in coming days if there is no fresh cash entry," he added.
Turkish markets await Treasury's 273-day bill auction on Tuesday and November inflation figures to be released on Wednesday to see direction of interest rates.

The Treasury issued small amounts of bills in the last three auctions between November 5 and 19 and raised the yields sharply due to weak demand caused by a 10 percent witholding tax imposed on interest income from bills and bonds issued after November 1.

Of the 228 shares traded, 86 advanced, 86 declined and 56 were unchanged. The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.72 percent to 97,593.06 while the 15-share financial index eased 0.28 percent to 88,667.27.

Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, steady at 14,500 lira, T.Isbank's C series which dropped 250 lira to 18,250 and foreign trade firm EGS Dis Ticaret which lost 500 lira to 20,000. Together, they made up 23.9 percent of the total turnover.
